title: Mathematical Statistics
curriculum_locator: Printed page 9, Stat H-202 Mathematical Statistics I; University of Dhaka four-year B.S. Honours Statistics curriculum, starting session 2023–2024

units.title: Foundations of Statistical Models, Parametric Families, Identifiability, and Likelihood Principles
scope: Statistical experiment spaces, Borel sample spaces, and probability measures
Parametric families of distributions and parameter spaces
Model identifiability and algebraic proofs of non-identifiable mixtures
The Likelihood Principle, profile likelihood, and score function algebra
Fisher Information regularity conditions and Cramér-Rao regularity assumptions
worked_questions: Proof of parameter identifiability in location-scale families and non-identifiable finite Gaussian mixture degeneracies
Derivation of the Score function, Fisher Information matrix, and Bartlett identities for truncated distributions
Profile likelihood derivation and relative profile curvature analysis for nuisance parameter elimination

units.title: Random Samples, Joint Distributions, Sampling Statistics, and Moment Generating Techniques
scope: Random sampling models and joint probability density factorizations
Sample statistics as Borel measurable transformations of sample vectors
Exact sampling distribution of linear combinations of independent random variables
Moment generating functions (MGF), characteristic functions, and uniqueness inversion theorems
Convolution integrals and Laplace transform techniques in sampling theory
worked_questions: Exact sampling distribution of the sum of independent Gamma variates with unequal scale parameters via MGF inversion
Joint distribution and independence of the sample mean and sample variance for non-Gaussian parent populations
Convolution integral derivation for the ratio and product of independent Cauchy and Uniform random variables

units.title: Normal-Sample Theory, Quadratic Forms, and Exact Sampling Distributions
scope: Multivariate normal distribution properties, affine transformations, and characteristic functions
Distribution of quadratic forms in normal vectors: idempotent matrices and Craig's theorem
Cochran's Theorem on the decomposition of sums of squares
Derivation of the Chi-Square, Student's t, and Snedecor-Fisher F distributions
Independence of the sample mean and sample variance in Gaussian populations
worked_questions: Full rigorous proof of Cochran's Theorem using matrix spectral decomposition and moment generating functions
Derivation of the exact probability density function of Student's t distribution with nu degrees of freedom
Distribution of the ratio of quadratic forms in Gaussian vectors and proof of Fisher-Snedecor F distribution properties

units.title: Order Statistics, Joint Densities, Extremes, Spacings, and Sample Quantiles
scope: Marginal distribution and exact probability density of the k-th order statistic
Joint probability density function of multiple order statistics
Distribution of sample range, midrange, and normalized spacings
Uniform order statistics and their Dirichlet and Beta marginals
Limiting distributions of sample extremes and the Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko theorem
worked_questions: Derivation of the joint distribution of the minimum and maximum order statistics and the exact density of the sample range for Uniform(0, theta)
Proof of independence and exponential distribution of normalized spacings from an Exponential parent population
Asymptotic normality proof of the sample median and sample p-th quantile using Bahadur representations

units.title: Data Reduction and Sufficiency: Factorization, Minimal Sufficiency, and Ancillarity
scope: The concept of data reduction and loss of information
Sufficient statistics and the Halmos-Savage / Fisher-Neyman Factorization Theorem
Minimal sufficient statistics and the Lehmann-Scheffé ratio partition technique
Ancillary statistics and first-order ancillarity
Basu's Theorem on the independence of complete sufficient statistics and ancillary statistics
worked_questions: Rigorous proof of the Fisher-Neyman Factorization Theorem for discrete and continuous sample spaces
Finding the two-dimensional minimal sufficient statistic for the normal distribution with unknown mean and variance using the Lehmann-Scheffé ratio criterion
Application of Basu's Theorem to prove the statistical independence of the sample variance and the sample coefficient of variation in normal populations

units.title: Exponential Families of Distributions: Natural Parameters, Completeness, and Information Bounds
scope: Standard and canonical (natural) representation of k-parameter Exponential Families
Natural parameter spaces, convexity, and steepness regularity conditions
Moments and cumulants via differentiation of the log-partition function A(eta)
Completeness and bounded completeness of natural sufficient statistics
Curved exponential families and geometry of the score manifold
worked_questions: Classification of the Beta, Gamma, and Multivariate Gaussian families into natural exponential form and verification of parameter space convexity
Derivation of the mean vector and covariance matrix of natural sufficient statistics through the gradient and Hessian of the log-partition function
Proof of completeness of the natural sufficient statistic in full-rank exponential families using Fourier inversion

units.title: Stochastic Convergence and Limit Theorems: Laws of Large Numbers and Central Limit Theorems
scope: Modes of stochastic convergence: in probability, in distribution, almost surely, and in r-th mean
Implications and counterexamples between convergence modes
The Weak Law of Large Numbers (WLLN): Chebyshev, Khinchin, and Kolmogorov conditions
The Strong Law of Large Numbers (SLLN): Borel-Cantelli lemmas and Kolmogorov's Strong Law
The Classical Lindeberg-Lévy Central Limit Theorem and Lindeberg-Feller condition
worked_questions: Rigorous hierarchy proof showing that almost sure convergence and L^r convergence imply convergence in probability, with counterexamples showing the converses fail
Proof of the Weak Law of Large Numbers under finite second moments and extension to Khinchin's theorem using characteristic functions
Verification of the Lindeberg condition for triangular arrays of independent non-identically distributed random variables

units.title: Asymptotic Distribution Theory: Continuous Mapping, Slutsky's Theorem, and the Delta Method
scope: The Continuous Mapping Theorem (Mann-Wald Theorem) for probability and distribution limits
Slutsky's Theorem: algebraic operations on sequences converging in distribution and probability
The Univariate Delta Method: Taylor series expansions and asymptotic variance propagation
The Multivariate Delta Method: Jacobian transformations and asymptotic covariance matrices
Asymptotic Relative Efficiency (ARE) and Pitman efficiency comparisons
worked_questions: Detailed step-by-step proof of Slutsky's Theorem using the portmanteau lemma and probabilistic bounds
Derivation of the asymptotic distribution of the sample coefficient of variation using the bivariate Delta Method
Asymptotic relative efficiency computation of the sample median relative to the sample mean for normal and Double Exponential (Laplace) distributions
